I intend to use, and have, a mounting cradle for the rifle, a set of levels for the scope, and a lazer bore site. I am inexperienced in this endeavor, any thoughts?

Shiiit yes. But I’ve limited time so bear with me

Scope rings — get the best you can find in the price range you can afford. It’s silly to spend dough on a good rifle and scope and then hose the interface with some flimsy shit. Torque them to spec, and if you can’t find spec, 18-20lb/ft will be a safe range, which means get a torque wrench. An inexpensive digital one will do because you aren’t Carlos Hathcock

Leveling — make sure your scope is perfectly level when torquing the rings and know that sometimes that last bit of torque exerts pressure which twists the scope just so. Make sure it’s true, and then get an attached scope level called a “cant indicator.” It will help you check at a glance if you have any sideways cant in your rifle that will blow your call. Getting dialed in is useless if the rifle is not positioned correctly at the time you pull the trigger

Laser bore sight — I’m meh about them because some are machined better and more precise, but I’d be dishonest if I told you I gave more than a fuckall about them. Boresight to get you on paper and then learn your scopes true dial adjustments. Higher cost will get you precision, while lower end may get you ballpark. Your scope on your rifle with your choice of ammo is all the truth you need
